papers.title: Clumps in a Cocoon: Geometry and Mixing Set the Universal X-ray to H$α$ Surface Brightness Ratio
papers.abstract: Recent observations reveal a nearly universal X-ray to H$\alpha$ surface-brightness ratio, ${\rm SB}_{\rm X}/{\rm SB}_{\rm H\alpha}\sim 3$, in galactic winds, ram-pressure-stripped tails, and cluster filaments. This is surprising, given the very different temperatures traced by the X-ray and H$\alpha$ emission. Plane-parallel mixing-layer models do not recover this ratio. We run 3D wind-tunnel simulations in the high density-contrast ($\chi\sim 10^3$) regime, where the cold phase shatters into small H$\alpha$-emitting clumps embedded in a volume-filling X-ray cocoon. After smoothing on the tail-width scale, the simulated ratio converges to the observed value. The hot-gas entrainment rate sets the bolometric luminosity, $L_{\rm bol} \propto \dot{M}_{\rm in}$. H$\alpha$ carries a nearly fixed fraction of this luminosity, set mainly by atomic emissivity near $10^4$ K. The X-ray-emitting mass is the same entrainment rate multiplied by the residence time in the X-ray-emitting temperature band, and its luminosity is the corresponding thermal energy divided by the cooling time. Hence $L_{\rm X} \propto \dot M_{\rm in} \propto L_{\rm bol}$, with the X-ray fraction set by the residence-to-cooling-time ratio. An age diagnostic constrains the residence time to be far shorter than the cooling time, making the X-ray and H$\alpha$ fractions comparable. Their common scaling with $L_{\rm bol}$ explains the correlation, while the comparable bolometric fractions explain why the observed ratio is order unity.
papers.comments: 7 pages, 3 figures. Accepted for publication in MNRAS Letters, 3 November 2026

papers.title: MusE GAs FLOw and Wind (MEGAFLOW) XIV: Background-Galaxy Absorption Reveals Kiloparsec-Scale Structure in the Cool Circumgalactic Medium
papers.abstract: The properties of the cool ($T\sim10^4$~K) gas in the circumgalactic medium (CGM) are closely linked to the physical mechanisms that create and maintain this multiphase medium. The cool CGM is thought to consist of discrete clouds, whose characteristic size is unknown. Here we present a geometric and direct approach to constrain the coherence scale of these cool structures using stacked MgII absorption lines measured against extended background galaxies and effectively point-like background quasars, whose sizes are a few kpc and $\lesssim 0.01$pc, respectively. When the background-source size is smaller than the coherence scale of the foreground clouds, incomplete covering lowers the detection fraction and causes the median stacked absorption to differ from the mean. For stacked MgII absorption against background galaxies, the mean and median equivalent width (EW) profiles are broadly consistent. For stacked MgII absorption against background quasars, by contrast, the median and mean EW profiles differ significantly, reaching a $\approx10\sigma$ difference beyond 100 kpc. Furthermore, we find that the median and mean EW profiles are broadly consistent for large background galaxies (median half-light radius $\approx 6.6$ kpc), but differ at the $\approx3\sigma$ level for small background galaxies ($\approx 1.5$ kpc). This suggests that the MgII-bearing gas has an effective transverse coherence scale of order a few kiloparsecs, broadly consistent with the $\sim$2--7 kpc range probed by the background galaxies. Using a toy model in which the CGM is populated with discrete cool clouds, we show that the observed differences arise naturally from the combination of partial covering and beam averaging. Our results provide a new geometry-based measure of the small-scale structure of cool CGM gas.
papers.comments: Accepted for publication in A&A

papers.title: Tachyonic Encore: A universal shift of inflationary observables
papers.abstract: We propose a generic mechanism applicable to single-field inflaton models in which a light axion spectator, initialized near the hilltop of its potential, reshapes inflationary observables through purely gravitational multi-field dynamics. During inflation the axion is frozen and the background follows an effectively single-field trajectory. After inflation ends, the axion rolls, inducing a turn in field space and transient tachyonic phases of the isocurvature mode. The resulting ``tachyonic encore'' occurs entirely on super-horizon scales. These phases generate a nearly scale-invariant enhancement of the curvature power spectrum, suppressing the tensor-to-scalar ratio and shifting the scalar tilt to a weighted combination of adiabatic and entropic tilts at horizon crossing. We show that these effects can reconcile otherwise disfavored inflaton potentials with current CMB constraints. The same dynamics predict local non-Gaussianity, $f_{\rm NL}^{\rm loc.}\sim \mathcal{O}(1)$, within reach of upcoming surveys.
papers.comments: 13 pages, 4 figures

papers.title: Revisiting the Lyth bound constraints on inflation from ACT DR6 results
papers.abstract: The Lyth bound asserts that the field excursion of inflaton must be sub-Planckian, thereby imposing an upper bound on the amplitude of the tensor power spectrum in inflationary scenario. This bound is conventionally derived assuming a scale-invariant curvature power spectrum, i.e., $n_s = 1$. However, astrophysical observations confirm a red-tilted spectrum with $n_s < 1$. In light of recent results from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) DR6, we revisit these constraints using the newly implied scalar spectral index of $n_s \simeq 0.9743$. Incorporating the ACT data yields a different upper bound on the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$, which can potentially exclude inflationary scenarios previously robust under the original Lyth bound with $n_s = 1$. Our result highlights the urgent need to combine theoretical Lyth bound considerations with the most up-to-date astrophysical data.
papers.comments: 23 pages, 5 figures,

papers.title: Primordial Black Holes from Vector-Induced Curvature Perturbations Sourced by Primordial Magnetic Fields
papers.abstract: Generating an appreciable abundance of primordial black holes (PBHs) requires a substantial enhancement of primordial curvature perturbations on small scales. In this Letter, we propose a new post-inflationary mechanism in which such an enhancement arises during a stiff, or kination, epoch. The mechanism is driven by metric vector perturbations sourced by the vector component of the electromagnetic stress-energy tensor associated with primordial magnetic fields (PMFs). Since these first-order vector modes remain approximately constant during kination, they act as persistent nonlinear sources for second-order scalar perturbations. We show that the resulting vector-induced curvature perturbations are amplified toward the infrared cutoff of the kination band and exhibit the characteristic scaling $\mathcal P_{\mathcal R}(k)\propto k^{-5}$. As a concrete realization, we consider PMFs generated in a Ratra-type magnetogenesis scenario and find that the induced curvature perturbations can produce PBHs with an abundance large enough to constitute a substantial fraction of the dark matter.
papers.comments: 13 pages, 2 figures. Accepted for publication in Physical Review D as a Letter

papers.title: Morpho-kinematic of galaxies at cosmic noon
papers.abstract: Recent studies of local galaxies highlight the need for high-resolution photometry and kinematics to accurately characterize galactic structures. From this, limitations emerged in the standard two-phase evolutionary scenario, where galaxies first form dispersion-supported bulges followed by secular disk growth. IFS surveys, combining photometry and kinematics, demonstrated that morphology and dynamics correlate weakly, with bulges and disks forming a continuum in their kinematic properties. This scenario is further supported by JWST observations. From analyses based on visual morphology emerged that mature galaxies with distinct morphological features exist at earlier times than expected. This, however, needs to be confirmed with high-resolution stellar kinematics observations. We, therefore, propose to measure stellar kinematics at high spatial resolution for massive galaxies at cosmic noon to probe the build-up of central regions and to disentangle the true nature of structures inferred from visual morphology (e.g., disks and bulges with different degrees of rotation). This will enable studying how galaxy mass, kinematics, and star formation co-evolve, providing a complete census of galactic structures and their formation pathways. In this regard, the VESPER-SHARP instrument on the E-ELT is uniquely suited for this program, offering, within reasonable exposure times, rest-frame optical coverage at $z\sim2$, high spatial resolution, a suitable field of view, and multiplexing for simultaneous observations.
papers.comments: 6 pages, 2 figures, accepted for publication on New Astronomy

papers.title: A new era for Dual AGN science with SHARP
papers.abstract: The search for and the characterization of ultra-compact dual active galactic nuclei (AGN) are among the hottest topics of current extragalactic astrophysics. These systems involve two accreting massive black holes (MBHs) embedded within the same host galaxy, with relative projected separations from a few hundred pc down to a few pc. They are central to understanding hierarchical galaxy formation, black hole growth and demographics, and accretion-feedback coupling in the most extreme interaction phases. Even more compellingly, such tight pairs are the most direct precursors of gravitationally bound binary MBHs (sub-pc scale separation), which are among the loudest emitters of gravitational waves (GWs) in the low-frequency ranges. SHARP will deliver the first statistical census and physical characterization of ultra-compact dual AGN up to cosmic distances, finally bridging the observational gap between kpc-scale pairs and sub-pc GW-emitting binaries, and enabling a breakthrough understanding of MBH growth, feedback and co-evolution across cosmic time.
papers.comments: 8 pages, 2 figures, Published in the New Astronomy Special issue: SHARP science book

papers.title: A SHARP Look at Quenching and Bulge-Disk Growth in Massive Galaxies at Cosmic Noon
papers.abstract: The physical mechanisms that quench star formation in massive galaxies remain poorly understood. At cosmic noon (1<z<3), when star formation and AGN activity peak, galaxies rapidly evolve from star-forming disks into quiescent, bulge-dominated systems. While quenching correlates with stellar mass and bulge growth, the causal link between bulge assembly, star-formation suppression, and feedback processes remains unclear. Stellar population analysis from spatially resolved spectroscopy of galaxies caught during quenching is crucial to advance on this issue. We show that the SHARP-VESPER Integral-Field Spectrograph (IFS) can efficiently fill this gap by combining ELT-class sensitivity, 31 mas spatial resolution (>3x sharper than JWST) and broad near-IR wavelength coverage with 12-IFU multiplexing. This will enable, for the first time, a simultaneous bulge-disk decomposition of stellar populations and spatially resolved mapping of ionised gas in massive galaxies (log $M_*/M_{\odot}\geq 11$) at 2.2<z<3.5, targeting systems on the main sequence shortly before quenching or already in the green valley. With typical exposure times of 15 hr, we will obtain S/N>15-20 per spectral resolution element, on the inner bulge, and outer disk extracted spectral continuum, and S/N>5 for nebular lines ([OII], H$\beta$, [OIII], H$\alpha$) on sub-kpc scales. These observations will allow us to reconstruct independent bulge and disk star-formation histories, ages, metallicities, and $\alpha$-enhancements, while mapping spatially resolved star formation, gas kinematics, and feedback-driven outflows. By directly comparing the timing of bulge growth and star-formation suppression across galaxy components, this programme will test whether quenching proceeds inside-out, distinguish fast and slow quenching pathways, and link structural transformation to feedback processes in the most massive galaxies at cosmic noon.
papers.comments: 13 pages, 1 figure, published in New Astronomy as part of Special Issue "SHARP Science Book"

papers.title: Probing IMF Variations in High-Redshift Early-Type Galaxies with SHARP
papers.abstract: The stellar initial mass function (IMF), which describes the distribution of stellar masses at birth, is a fundamental ingredient in shaping galaxy evolution. Recent observations indicate that the IMF varies between galaxies, depending on their mass, morphology, and stellar content. In local early-type galaxies (ETGs), spectroscopy, dynamics, and lensing reveal bottom-heavy IMFs in dense central regions, with radial gradients toward a Milky Way-like distribution in the outskirts. Yet, the chemical enrichment of massive ETGs implies a dominant role of massive stars during their early formation phases. These findings can be reconciled if the IMF evolves over cosmic time -- initially more top-heavy to enable rapid enrichment, and later dominated by long-lived, low-mass stars. Directly measuring the IMF at z>1 is therefore essential to test such time-dependent IMF scenarios, including variations in the dwarf-to-giant and stellar mass-to-light ratios. To date, no direct observational confirmation of these IMF variations -- or of their physical origin -- has been obtained. The SHARP spectrograph on the E-ELT, with unprecedented spatial resolution and sensitivity compared to facilities such as JWST, and broader spectral coverage than other E-ELT instruments, will enable spatially resolved spectroscopy of IMF-sensitive features in high-redshift ETGs up to z~3, providing unique insights into the origin of the non-universal IMF in massive galaxies.
papers.comments: Accepted for publication in New Astronomy as a contribution to the SHARP Science Book

papers.title: Precision Solar System Dynamics for Ultralight Dark Matter Search
papers.abstract: Ultralight dark matter exhibits an order-one density fluctuation at the scale of its wavelength. This density fluctuation exists across the entire dark matter halo and interacts with stars and planets, perturbing their motion via gravitational interactions. We investigate the possibility of using precision solar system dynamics to search for ultralight dark matter. We examine this possibility with interplanetary radio range measurements. We show that the precision of current range measurements can probe ultralight dark matter at masses around $10^{-15}\,$eV, had its density in the solar system been $10^5$ larger than the so-called local dark matter density. This limit complements other constraints, such as the one from analyses of pulsar timing observations.
papers.comments: 24 pages, 8 figures; v2: matches published version

papers.title: Fast Graph-based Higher-Order Clustering Statistics on the GPU
papers.abstract: We present a significant update to GRAMSCI (GRAph Made Statistics for Cosmological Information; Sabiu et al. 2019), an algorithm for the fast computation of the general $N$-point spatial correlation function of any discrete point set. Version 2 adds several features. We replace the binary-search inner loop ($O(m\log m)$ per hub-spoke pair, $m$ being the mean neighbor count) with a merge-walk algorithm that reduces the inner loop to $O(m)$. We implement a parity-decomposed 4pCF that separates the signal into even and odd channels. We estimate the disconnected 4pCF internally on the same graph to return the connected 4pCF. We add a Python/NumPy interface to the Fortran engine. Principally, we present a GPU port of the full query engine (OpenACC): the 3pCF, 4pCF, and parity-decomposed 4pCF kernels run on a single consumer GPU with measured speedups of $2.6\times$ (3pCF) to $9\times$ (4pCF) over a 64-thread CPU node, and out-of-core tiling handles graphs exceeding device memory. We measure a $9\times10^9$-edge BAO-scale 3pCF on a 24 GB card with $\sim 20\%$ overhead. We validate the code against its CPU reference, against analytic injection tests, and on exactly solvable random fields (a non-Gaussian multiplicative cascade and a Gaussian field, whose full and connected 4pCF the estimators reproduce without bias), and demonstrate BAO-scale applications on the DESI DR1 LRG sample (the 3pCF and the full and connected 4pCF over the complete configuration space, both to 150 $h^{-1}$ Mpc).
papers.comments: 23 pages, 12 figures, accepted in ApJS, code available from this https URL

papers.title: Gravitational Wave Birefringence in generalized Palatini Chern Simons
papers.abstract: The cosmological propagation of gravitational waves (GWs) can exhibit amplitude and phase polarization distortions when parity symmetry is broken, a phenomenon known as cosmological birefringence. In this paper, we investigate the phenomenology of GW birefringence in a gravitational model $f(R)$ coupled to a dynamical Chern-Simons (dCS) term, analyzed in the metric and Palatini formalisms. At the background level, this model can lead to dynamical dark energy, while for GW propagation we find that the Palatini formalism predicts both amplitude and velocity birefringence, whereas the metric formalism predicts amplitude birefringence only. We also find that the birefringence effects can either be suppressed or enhanced by the $f(R)$ interactions, depending on the specific form of $f(R)$. Considering three common $f(R)$ models (Hu-Sawicki, Exponential, and Hyperbolic gravity) fit to recent cosmological data, we find that birefringence is enhanced relative to the $f(R) = R$ case, by $1-10\%$ in the Palatini formalism and up to a factor of 2 in the metric formalism. We also translate current GW birefringence constraints to bounds on the dCS coupling within our model. Finally, we show that in our model the birefringence effect grows polynomially with source redshift, in contrast to the linear-distance scaling commonly assumed in phenomenological models of GW birefringence in the current literature.
papers.comments: 22 pages, 1 figure. Published version

papers.title: Inferring Properties of Rotating Core-Collapse Supernovae with Gravitational-Wave Detector Networks
papers.abstract: Core-collapse supernovae are among the most promising yet still undetected sources of gravitational waves. A future detection would provide a direct view of the physical processes occurring deep inside a collapsing star. In this work, we investigate how networks of current and future gravitational-wave detectors can constrain the properties of rapidly rotating core-collapse supernovae using their characteristic core-bounce and early post-bounce signals. Using deep-learning techniques, we estimate the peak frequency, rotation rate, and signal amplitude from noisy detector data and compare the performance of different detector-network configurations. We find that detector networks improve both parameter recovery and sky coverage. For current-generation networks, estimation of the peak frequency is possible out to about 15 kpc, while the rotation rate remains recoverable out to distances exceeding 100 kpc. Third-generation observatories extend these distances by approximately a factor of three to four.
papers.comments: Accepted for publication in PRD

papers.title: Probing the dynamics of extreme galaxies I. Dark matter content in ultra-diffuse galaxies
papers.abstract: We investigate the internal structure of two galaxies from the LEWIS sample: the ultra-diffuse galaxy UDG-1 and the extended dwarf LSB-6. Both show coherent stellar rotation combined with a non-negligible fraction of random motion, with no signs of ongoing disturbance. This is the first attempt to constrain the dynamics and dark matter physics of rotation-supported UDGs through integral-field stellar kinematics. We model the galaxies as stellar spheroids with typical dwarf-like thickness embedded in spherical dark matter halos, deriving two-dimensional velocity fields that we compare with the observations in a Bayesian framework. Besides cold dark matter, we test fuzzy, self-interacting, and non-minimally coupled dark matter. The data prefer a cuspy halo in UDG-1 and a cuspless one in LSB-6. All the alternative models remain viable, although current data cannot conclusively discriminate among them. For fuzzy dark matter we obtain mutually consistent boson masses, $m_\alpha = 4.7^{+1.8}_{-1.1} \times 10^{-22}$ eV for UDG-1 and $m_\alpha = 6.3^{+0.4}_{-0.4} \times 10^{-22}$ eV for LSB-6. For self-interacting dark matter, LSB-6 yields a robust constraint on the velocity-weighted cross section, $\langle \sigma v\rangle/m = 14.3^{+2.0}_{-1.9}$ cm$^2$ km g$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$. For non-minimally coupled dark matter we derive upper bounds on the coupling length, implying marginal deviations from $\Lambda$CDM. Regardless of the model, both galaxies exhibit a dark matter content comparable with halos of typical dwarf galaxies with similar stellar masses. Together with stellar population analyses and globular cluster information, these results support a scenario in which UDG-1 and LSB-6 originate from puffed-up dwarfs. This work is the first in a series exploiting kinematic data of extremely low-surface-brightness galaxies to test fundamental physics, from dark matter to modified theories of gravity.
papers.comments: 26 pages, 13 figures, 3 tables

papers.title: Stellar bar occurrence in TNG50 and TNG100: disentangling environmental effects and assembly history at z = 0
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate the dependence of bar presence on environment using TNG50 and TNG100 simulations at z=0. We select disc galaxies within $2 R_{200}$, with stellar mass M$_{\star} \geq 10^{10}$ M$_{\odot}$ (TNG100) and M$_{\star} \geq 10^{9}$ M$_{\odot}$ (TNG50). With these criteria, our final samples consist of 1719 and 859 satellite galaxies in TNG100 and TNG50, respectively. The environment is characterised by host halo mass: massive (M$_{\rm h} \geq 10^{14}$ M$_{\odot}$), intermediate ($10^{13} < \rm M_{\rm h} < 10^{14}$ M$_{\odot}$), and low-mass haloes (M$_{\rm h} \leq 10^{13}$ M$_{\odot}$). We find that our samples recover the morphology-density relation, with thin disc fractions increasing with cluster-centric distance and decreasing halo mass. The bar fraction and the bar radius normalized by the effective radius decrease mildly with cluster-centric distance, while absolute bar radii remain constant. At fixed distance, the bar fraction increases with halo mass, partly because more massive galaxies reside in more massive haloes. In addition, we find that galaxies with earlier assembly times show a higher bar fraction, especially within $0.5 R_{200}$, suggesting a connection between earlier assembly and a higher probability of hosting a bar. Overall, we find a mild environmental dependence, with a stronger connection to stellar mass and assembly history.
papers.comments: 16 pages, 13 figures, accepted for publication in MNRAS

papers.title: Thermodynamic topology of magnetic GMGHS black holes: the $\overline {W}^{1-}$ subclass
papers.abstract: Thermodynamic topology provides a topological classification of black hole states and their branch structures in thermodynamic parameter space. We investigate the thermodynamic topology of the charged nonextremal magnetic Gibbons--Maeda family in four-dimensional asymptotically flat Einstein--Maxwell--dilaton gravity, with particular emphasis on its string-theory member at the dilaton coupling $a=1$, the Gibbons--Maeda--Garfinkle--Horowitz--Strominger (GMGHS) black hole. An analytic classification over the complete domain of regular outer horizons shows that the dilaton coupling separates the family into three limiting structures of the inverse Hawking temperature. At $a=1$, the GMGHS defect curve approaches a nonzero lower inverse temperature endpoint and contains a single unstable branch. In particular, the magnetic GMGHS black hole provides an explicit realization of the previously proposed $\overline W^{1-}$ thermodynamic topological subclass within an asymptotically flat Einstein--Maxwell--dilaton solution. This result demonstrates that the global topological number $W$ alone does not completely characterize black hole thermodynamic topology. The asymptotic behavior of the inverse Hawking temperature near the boundaries of the physical horizon domain provides an additional criterion for distinguishing thermodynamic topological subclasses with the same $W$.
papers.comments: 11 pages, 3 figures; accepted version by EPJC

papers.title: A derived evolution of dark energy from cosmic inhomogeneity confronted with baryon acoustic oscillations and type Ia supernovae
papers.abstract: The volume dynamics of space is a framework in which the possibility that matter can be unevenly distributed enters the expansion dynamics directly. It yields a redshift-dependent effective Hubble constant and dark-energy density parameter from the Planck parameters alone. We derive the expansion history $H(z)$ of the framework and show that it is flat $\Lambda$CDM with the cosmological constant replaced by a dark-energy density that grows by 31 percent toward the present, with an effective equation of state $w(0) = -1.21$ approaching $-1$ at high redshift and a present-day age of 13.52 Gyr, 0.3 Gyr younger than in the homogeneous limit. We confront it with the DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations and the Pantheon+ type Ia supernovae, with the Hubble constant, the sound horizon and the supernova absolute magnitude free, so that only the shape of $H(z)$ is tested. Relative to $\Lambda$CDM the prediction is disfavored by $\Delta\chi^2 = 65$ with one parameter fewer. A free matter density reduces this to $\Delta\chi^2 = 42$, because each probe alone accommodates the model only with incompatible matter densities (0.35 from the oscillations, 0.54 from the supernovae). Their combination bounds the heterogeneity amplitude to $\sigma_8 < 0.14$ at 95 percent confidence, against the Planck input 0.81; the best fit of the heterogeneous model is its homogeneous limit, flat $\Lambda$CDM. At the leading order currently evaluated, the heterogeneous contribution cannot account for the Hubble tension, and it acts opposite to the evolution of dark energy that current distance data favor.
papers.comments: 11 pages, 3 figures. Submitted to Eur. Phys. J. C. v5: minor corrections

papers.title: An ALMA sub-kiloparsec test of the Kennicutt--Schmidt relation in a strongly lensed dusty star-forming galaxy at $z\sim2.78$
papers.abstract: [abridged] Star formation is a key process driving galaxy evolution, but understanding how it proceeds within the interstellar medium (ISM) requires resolving cold molecular gas and dust on sub-kpc scales. At z~2-3, near the peak of cosmic star formation, such resolution can generally only be achieved through strong gravitational lensing. We present an ALMA study of SMMJ0658, a 20x-magnified main-sequence star-forming galaxy at z=2.7768 +/- 0.0002, lensed by the Bullet Cluster (z=0.296) into three images. We use 0.2" and 0.6" ALMA Band-3 observations to test the Kennicutt-Schmidt (KS) relation at sub-kpc scales at cosmic noon. Using a JWST-based strong-lensing model of the Bullet Cluster, we reconstruct source-plane CO(3-2) and rest-frame 803um dust-continuum maps down to ~200pc scales. We derive spatially resolved molecular gas and star formation rate surface densities, depletion times, and the scale dependence of the CO-to-dust flux ratio over 200pc-3.2kpc apertures. The 0.2" ALMA data reveal massive, dense star-forming clumps, with Sigma_mol ~1.3-2.3 x 10^3 M_sun pc^-2, Sigma_SFR ~0.5-2.3 M_sun yr^-1 kpc^-2, and tau_dep ~0.82-2.56 Gyr. CO-dust spatial decorrelation produces a strong scale dependence in tau_dep. We find a KS-relation breakdown scale of 0.8 +/- 0.1 kpc, consistent with individual regions tracing distinct stages of the star-formation cycle. The ALMA and JWST data also reveal evidence for a lensed galaxy pair at z~2.78, although whether SMMJ0658 is undergoing an early-stage interaction remains uncertain. Our results show that the apparent universality of the KS relation breaks down once individual star-forming regions are spatially resolved, in line with observations from the local universe to z~1. We extend this picture to z~2.78, providing new insight into the resolved properties of the clumpy cold ISM and the star-formation cycle at cosmic noon.
papers.comments: Accepted for publication in A&A (18 pages, 15 figures, 4 tables)

papers.title: Boosted Odds: Lower-Point Probes of Parity Violation with Momentum Fields
papers.abstract: Parity-violating initial conditions are uniquely compelling signatures of inflationary dynamics beyond the single-field slow-roll paradigm, and their effects on the distribution of late-time observables can be easily separated from that of gravitational nonlinearities and galaxy formation physics. In this work, we propose using the momentum field, $\mathbf{p} = (1+\delta)\mathbf{v}$, and, in particular, the density-density-momentum bispectrum as a novel probe of primordial parity violation. This class of bispectra greatly complements traditional searches using four-point statistics of the density field, furnishing new observables that can be sensitive to parity-violating physics. At the same time, its lower dimensionality substantially reduces the complexity associated with analysing high-dimensional data vectors and their covariance. We show that the sensitivity of the density-density-momentum bispectrum to parity violation effects persists even if we can only observe the projection of the momentum field along the line-of-sight. We perform a Fisher forecast for the parity-violating amplitude of the ultra-squeezed template in the cross bispectrum of kinetic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (kSZ) anisotropies and galaxy clustering, and we find that our approach give competitive constraints when compared to existing methods. Our method can be easily co-opted to existing pipelines to study parity violation and, as the galaxy-galaxy-kSZ bispectrum is a key cosmological probe, take advantage of the significant existing efforts dedicated to mitigating systematics and covariance modelling.
papers.comments: 45 pages of text and 7 figures. Added references and minor changes

papers.title: Beyond the Disc--Spheroid Dichotomy at $0.6 < z < 8.0$: Evidence for a Morphological Indeterminacy Regime from JWST
papers.abstract: Galaxy morphology is a fundamental tracer of galaxy assembly, but its characterization becomes increasingly uncertain in the early Universe. We investigate morphological classifications across different methodologies over the redshift range $0.6 < z < 8.0$, using JWST observations of 15,567 galaxies with 6,099 synthetic galaxies from IllustrisTNG. To quantify morphology without relying on visual labels or prescribed light profiles, we use an unsupervised-supervised hybrid machine-learning approach based on the non-parametric MEGG system, which combines the second moment of the light distribution, Entropy, Gini, and Gradient Pattern Analysis. We find that parametric and non-parametric classifications remain broadly consistent at $z < 2.5$, but diverge systematically at higher redshift. We identify this epoch as the Morphological Indeterminacy Regime (MIR), in which classical disc and spheroidal categories no longer provide a unique description of the galaxy population. The fraction of mixed-interpretation galaxies increases with redshift, reaching $F_{\rm MIR} \sim 0.55$ at $z > 2.5$. Cross-domain and projection-invariance tests show that the classifications are stable and insensitive to data set and viewing angle. In the interval $2.5 < z < 8.0$, MIR galaxies occupy an intermediate stellar-mass regime (median; $\log(M_\star/M_\odot) \sim 9.7$), between low-mass discs (median; $\log(M_\star/M_\odot) \sim 9.5$) and massive spheroids (median; $\log(M_\star/M_\odot) \sim 10.1$), while irregular systems have stellar-mass distributions similar to those of MIR galaxies. We interpret these results as evidence that morphological indeterminacy is a characteristic feature of galaxy assembly in the early Universe, reflecting a population of dynamically young systems that have not yet settled into the classical Hubble sequence.
papers.comments: 14 pages, 10 figures. Submitted to Open Journal of Astrophysics (OJAp)

papers.title: Grey-body factors of black holes
papers.abstract: Grey-body factors describe the frequency-dependent transmission of fields through the effective potential generated by a black hole or another compact object. They convert the idealized thermal spectrum of Hawking radiation into the spectrum measured by an observer, determine absorption and scattering cross sections, and provide real-frequency observables complementary to quasinormal modes. In this review, we present a unified account of grey-body factors in black-hole physics and related systems. We formulate the scattering problem for asymptotically flat, de Sitter, and anti-de Sitter spacetimes, and discuss the connections between transmission coefficients, absorption cross sections, Hawking radiation, and ringdown. We also review methods for their computation and survey recent developments, including the correspondence between grey-body factors and quasinormal modes, their stability under deformations of the effective potential, wormhole transmission and superradiance, and their behavior in modified theories of gravity. Finally, we discuss the appearance of grey-body factors in gauge/gravity duality, where absorption probabilities in the bulk are related to correlation functions and transport coefficients in the boundary theory.
papers.comments: Invited review for Reports on Progress in Physics

papers.title: Unveiling the nonthermal environments of NGC 3411 and NGC 5903 through new MeerKAT observations
papers.abstract: Galaxy groups are key laboratories for investigating the interplay between active galactic nucleus (AGN) outbursts and the dynamical processes of the intra-group medium. We aim to characterize the morphology, spectral properties, and magnetic field structure of the diffuse nonthermal radio emission in two peculiar galaxy groups, NGC 3411 and NGC 5903, selected from an originally larger sample, in order to constrain its origin and its connection with the dynamics of the intra-group medium. We present new MeerKAT UHF- and L-band observations of the two groups, complemented by archival Chandra and XMM-Newton data already analyzed in previous works. In NGC 3411, we detect extended radio emission surrounding the central AGN over scales of ~70 kpc, and resolve previously undetected arc-shaped substructures on scales of ~20-30 kpc. This extended component exhibits a relatively uniform steep spectrum ($\alpha$ ~ -1.7). We discuss possible scenarios for its origin, including mini-halos, aged AGN plasma, weak shocks, and the possibility of a radio galaxy observed along the line of sight. In NGC 5903, MeerKAT reveals a complex filamentary morphology, including a previously unknown ring-like structure surrounding the central AGN. Spectral-index mapping shows localized flattening ($\alpha$ ~ -0.9) along the north arc, while polarization data reveal ordered magnetic fields and a patchy rotation measure distribution across the source. Together with the disturbed X-ray morphology, these results support a scenario in which fossil AGN plasma has been redistributed and locally reenergized by group-scale dynamical processes such as turbulence, shear, and weak compression. Our results demonstrate that galaxy groups can host a rich variety of nonthermal phenomena, whose properties can only be fully revealed through the combination of sensitive, high-resolution, and multifrequency radio observations.

papers.title: Realistic neutron stars in the constant-Q branch of f(Q) gravity
papers.abstract: We investigate the hydrostatic equilibrium and global structure of neutron stars within symmetric teleparallel gravity, where gravitational interactions are mediated by the non-metricity scalar $Q$. Working within the metric-affine formulation, we adopt the regular, constant-$Q$ branch ($Q = Q_*$) of $f(Q)$ gravity, which preserves regularity at the stellar centre while maintaining explicit dependence on the non-linear functional form through $f(Q_*)$ and its derivatives. We propose three novel non-linear $f(Q)$ extensions: (i) a Born-Infeld-inspired model, (ii) a Hu--Sawicki analogue, and (iii) a Tsujikawa-inspired model. Incorporating state-of-the-art realistic unified equations of state, namely GPPVA(DD2) and SLy4, we numerically solve the modified Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations and evaluate stellar stability via the Harrison-Zel'dovich-Novikov criterion. The Born-Infeld and Hu-Sawicki analogues smoothly recover the general relativistic limit as their control parameters increase, predicting stellar radii for low-mass objects ($M < 2.0\,M_\odot$) that match observational constraints from X-ray binaries and GW170817; however, their maximum masses remain capped below $2.43\,M_\odot$ (DD2) and $2.06\,M_\odot$ (SLy4). Conversely, the Tsujikawa-inspired model significantly stiffens the effective gravitational coupling, accommodating massive compact objects up to $\sim 3.36\,M_\odot$ and offering a viable physical origin for the $2.59_{-0.09}^{+0.08}\,M_\odot$ secondary object in GW190814, albeit at the expense of overpredicting radii for typical low-mass neutron stars. These contrasting behaviours demonstrate a key phenomenological complementarity between maximum mass and radius bounds within the constant-$Q$ framework, highlighting the utility of multimessenger observations in constraining non-linear non-metricity gravity.
papers.comments: 19 pages, 4 figures (Further investigation added)

papers.title: Rotation overcharges vectorized black holes
papers.abstract: A charged black hole has a ceiling: extremality bounds the charge that a given mass and spin can support. Vector hair has so far only lowered it. In the Einstein--Maxwell--Vector (EMV) model, where a massless vector field couples nonminimally to the electromagnetic invariant, the spherically symmetric vectorized Reissner--Nordström black holes are strictly undercharged: vector hair is paid for in charge. Whether this ceiling is a property of the vector field or merely of spherical symmetry has remained open, because spherical symmetry hides the hair's mass as well: its Komar mass vanishes identically and the exact identity $M_V=2\Omega_HJ_V$ degenerates to $0=0$. Rotation lifts both degeneracies at once. We construct the rotating solutions of the model, the first in this setting, and find that the hair's mass is not a free parameter but a second-order invariant of the rotational response, fixed by $M_V=2\Omega_HJ_V$. Above a coupling threshold the ceiling gives way: the domain of existence crosses the extremal Kerr--Newman bound, reaching $q=Q/M>1$ with $q^2+\chi^2$ up to $1.84$, while at $\alpha=5$ the maximum charge stays below it. The shadow is where the hair becomes visible. At $(q,\chi)=(0.9947,0.10)$, near the extremal bound, the hair contributes an ellipticity of $8.30\%$, against $0.44\%$ from the charge and $0.06\%$ from rotation --- a factor of $19$ that charging a Kerr black hole cannot mimic; at the overcharged solution $(q,\chi)=(1.2527,0.10)$ the total ellipticity reaches $25.6\%$. Whether the branch is ghost-free remains open, but the existing no-go criteria do not settle it: they assume a background and a dispersion relation that do not hold here.
papers.comments: 19 pages, 11 figures
